A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLRE study. Full text and rendered-page comparison cover all 31 pages, including Figures 1-3, Tables 1-12, and Appendices A-H, without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original MT-Bench and Arena-Hard experiments, transferability and detectability tests, ablations, and human evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the detailed results and qualitative analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same RLRE pipeline, frozen candidate and judge models, contrastive loss, and preamble-generation procedure. No method components change.

E1.justification: Training remains on UltraFeedback, with evaluation on MT-Bench and Arena-Hard. Task domains, candidate/judge transfer scenarios, and human-study coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same no-attack control and verbosity, bandwagon, authority, refinement, and universal-adversarial baselines. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported splits, metrics, model configurations, training settings, and human-evaluation procedures are identical. The confidence-level wording correction does not introduce a different evaluation design.

E4.justification: The transferability and detectability tests, prompting ablations, accuracy and human-quality analyses, random-string control, and representative examples are retained unchanged, including Appendices G-H.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1 changes '90% confidence intervals' to '95%', resolving v2's disagreement with Table 10's existing 95% caption and column heading. Paired bootstrapping, interval endpoints, and repeated-run reporting remain unchanged; no recalculation or additional runs are reported.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, qualitative findings, and confidence-interval endpoints are unchanged. For example, Table 2's overall preamble scores remain 7.93 for Command R7B, 8.18 for Command R, and 8.22 for Llama 3.1 70B Instruct.

T1.justification: Section 3's expected-reward objective, contrastive loss, and mathematical definitions are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's six contributions, and conclusion retain identical claims about attack effectiveness, detectability, transferability, and broader RLRE applicability.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning score inflation versus answer quality, formatting bias, preamble fluency, computational constraints, and transferability remain unchanged. Appendix D.3 retains the same qualification of the Arena-Hard GPT-4 results.

D1.justification: Hardware, API model identifiers, hyperparameters, training-cost estimates, dataset identifiers, prompt templates, and annotation guidelines are unchanged. Both versions retain the same policy of withholding trained generator checkpoints.

R1.justification: No cited works or research-positioning arguments change. Reference [3] updates the same Bavaresco et al. study from its 2024 preprint to its ACL 2025 publication; other reference edits concern bibliographic metadata and capitalization.

P1.justification: Limited editorial changes update the version/date stamp, bibliography metadata and capitalization, and Appendix D.1's confidence-level wording. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded publication entry for reference [3] changes line wrapping and page breaks within the bibliography on pages 11-16. Figures, tables, captions, and appendix example layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves a concrete ambiguity in statistical reporting by making Appendix D.1 agree with Table 10's 95% confidence-level labels. Updated publication details also improve the bibliography. These are limited reporting improvements; the methods, experimental evidence, and substantive conclusions remain unchanged.
